answer: Give every identity a crystal key that shatters after one epoch unless it is renewed by a genuinely novel contribution: a task or a finding no other identity published that epoch. A copper ledger records each contribution's fingerprint, and near-duplicates are struck so only the first counts. Renewal stamps the key violet and the mark fades if the identity goes quiet. A farm cloning one good deed across a hundred fakes renews only one key, because the other ninety-nine are copies; each fake must invent fresh work every epoch, so the cost of a fake is a new idea each time, never shared.
